protocol.selectionRule: Lens Formula IDs 002,003,005,009,011 fixed before opening their images. Retain the resulting mix; do not cherry-pick for native success.
protocol.coverageCaution: Five cases from one section are not representative. These files were newly opened in this trial; earlier project-wide exposure cannot be excluded.
protocol.note: First interpretation preserved before new workflow execution. Conditional mathematical deductions are assistant reasoning, not measured native results. No corresponding Solutions image was opened.

cases.question: Convex lens gives an image of three times object size for object distances 16 cm and 8 cm. Find focal length.
cases.requestedResult: focal length from two magnification conditions
stated: absolute magnification 3 at distances 16 cm and 8 cm
derived: Under thin-lens geometric optics, the farther position gives inverted real magnification -3 and the nearer position upright virtual magnification +3; both imply f=12 cm.
Choose the lens at x=0 and incident propagation along +x. Two static demonstrations use source x=-16 and -8 cm.
unknowns: object height and whether it is a point emitter
cases.reason: The requested inverse focal-length solution is not a native observable. Two separately declared representative point-source scenes can check conditional ideal magnifications after the derivation; they do not simulate a moving extended object.
authorAssumptions: Represent one object point by a luminous point at y=+1 cm only for illustration; object height/emissivity were not supplied.
Use the documented opt-in aperture, emission and brightness choices; these are physical assumptions, not inferred facts.

cases.question: Plano-convex lens with convex radius 10 cm and focal length 30 cm; determine material refractive index.
derived: The conditional thin-lens lensmaker relation in air would give n=1+10/30=4/3. This relation is not implemented by the current ideal-lens adapter.
unknowns: surrounding medium and thickness assumptions not explicit
cases.reason: Current ideal-lens components store focal length, not material index or curved refracting surfaces. Do not substitute a fixed-focal-length scene for the requested material inference.

cases.question: A glass biconvex lens has n=1.6 and focal length 10 cm in air. Find focal lengths in media n=1.5 and n=1.7.
derived: Assuming thin-lens lensmaker scaling, f_medium=10*(1.6-1)/(1.6/n_medium-1) cm gives +90 cm and -102 cm. This is an external conditional calculation, not current native capability.
cases.reason: A fixed ideal focal length cannot simulate changing refractive media. Entering the analytically derived focal lengths would illustrate an equivalent surrogate, not execute the original material problem.

cases.question: A convex lens 45 cm above an empty tank bottom forms an image 36 cm above the lens. With liquid depth 40 cm the image is 48 cm above the lens; find liquid index.
cases.requestedResult: liquid refractive index from changed image position
derived: The initial ideal thin-lens subproblem gives f=45*36/(45+36)=20 cm.
Choose +x along upward propagation, lens x=0, bottom point x=-45 cm, y=0. A rigid coordinate-frame choice is not a gravity model.
unknowns: liquid index is the inverse unknown
cases.reason: The complete problem requires a plane refracting interface and inverse index determination, neither exposed by the current contract. Execute only the explicitly labelled empty-tank baseline; do not hide liquid refraction in a moved source.
authorAssumptions: Treat the stated point as a luminous probe on the optical axis for the empty-tank illustration only.
Apply the documented opt-in aperture/emission/brightness choices.

request.title: H4: EMPTY TANK ONLY; liquid problem unsupported

cases.question: A convex lens f1 images a luminous point at the shortest possible distance; a weak concave lens f2 is placed in contact. Find image shift.
cases.requestedResult: symbolic shift after adding a contact lens
stated: concave lens of very large focal length f2 placed in contact
unknowns: whether shortest distance means object-image separation or image-lens distance
cases.reason: The numeric authoring contract cannot accept unresolved symbols and disallows coincident lens planes. Do not invent a separation or merge the two physical lenses silently. Clarify the optimization statement before a symbolic analytic reduction; no native scene is authored.
